references.text: The psalmist describes enemies who lurk and watch every step—the same motif as in Luke 11:54, where the scribes and Pharisees lie in ambush to catch Jesus in something he says. [ref:Ps 56:6|Psalms 56:6]
The psalmist complains about enemies who "lie in ambush" against his life, just as Jesus' opponents lurked around him to trap him with his words. [ref:Ps 59:3|Psalms 59:3]

Jeremiah describes how his friends lurked around him to see if he would say something they could use against him—the same dynamic that the Pharisees and scribes exercised toward Jesus. [ref:Jer 20:10|Jeremiah 20:10]
The Pharisees made plans to catch Jesus in his words (ἐν λόγῳ), a parallel to Luke 11:54 where they try to "catch something from his mouth". [ref:Matt 22:15|Matthew 22:15]
They sent some Pharisees and Herodians to Jesus to catch him in his words—a close parallel to the ambush strategy in [ref:Luk 11:54|Luke 11:54]. [ref:Mark 12:13|Mark 12:13]
Early in Jesus' ministry, the scribes and Pharisees watched him closely to find something to accuse him of—the same motif expressed in [ref:Luk 11:54|Luke 11:54]. [ref:Luk 6:7|Luke 6:7]

They kept a close watch on him and sent out people who pretended to be sincere, hoping to catch him in something he said—a direct parallel to the trapping tactics in [ref:Luk 11:54|Luke 11:54]. [ref:Luk 20:20|Luke 20:20]
Luke uses the same Greek word ἐνεδρεύοντες for those who lay in ambush against Paul, just as the Pharisees lurked around Jesus in [ref:Luk 11:54|Luke 11:54]. [ref:Apg 23:21|Acts 23:21]
